title: Port Markdown viewer and low-ceremony editing parity
goal: Port the old Markdown viewer, artifact renderer compatibility, inline manual editing, autosave draft capture, and proposal-review lens behavior into the standalone app.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility rendering preserves old Markdown reader behavior
Editable manual documents support whole-section inline edits: clicking any editable paragraph/list/heading selects the logical section, not only the individual block
A logical editable section is bounded by its heading and the next same-or-higher-level heading, with the section body editable as one low-ceremony region
Toolbar block controls operate inside the active section; H2/H3/H4 controls can create or split sections instead of only changing one selected paragraph
Structured policy rules are enforced before a draft is captured, including allowed heading levels, section hierarchy, and non-editable static/regulatory content boundaries
Manual edits autosave to draft review instead of using per-section save/cancel ceremony
Draft review reuses the proposal-review lens shape
Model proposals remain separate at input time but converge into the same review/audit output
non_goals: Building every artifact as polished React components immediately
validation: Compare rendered samples against the old browser
Smoke inline edit draft capture and draft review

technical_defaults.summary: Build real workflow behavior before spending the last polish pass on cosmetics.
details: Treat the SG-0003 layout as good enough for the workflow build.
Allow small style/layout fixes when real edit, draft, or review states require them.
Defer broad visual refinement until persistent workflow states exist and can be judged on screen.

technical_defaults.summary: Use logical sections as the edit unit, with narrow block controls inside the section.
details: Clicking a paragraph, list item, H2, H3, or H4 should select the enclosing section.
The highlight/lens should cover the heading plus the section body, not a tiny one-block rectangle.
The block type controls remain available, but they edit or create blocks inside the active section.
Inserting H2/H3/H4 creates a new section boundary at the cursor or splits the active section.
Invalid hierarchy transitions should be prevented or captured as validation messages before draft review.
The normal UI should expose policy structure without turning into a raw Markdown editor.

technical_defaults.summary: Persist draft workflow state through the local service boundary.
details: Do not make the normal reader a raw Markdown editor.
Keep canonical Markdown unchanged until a later reviewed apply step.
Use service-backed draft/review state so reloads and future audit/history work have a durable seam.

technical_defaults.summary: Keep manual edits and model proposals separate at intake but converged at review output.
details: Manual section edits should autosave into draft review without per-section save/cancel ceremony.
Model proposal previews should remain distinct while being authored.
Both paths should converge on the same old/new lens-style review and future audit/apply shape.

prep_summary.resolved_human_choice: Use the accepted SG-0003 layout as the structural baseline, but restore the old section-level editing model before accepting SG-0014.
handoff: Start from the visible assistant/edit/draft-review affordances added in SG-0003.
Replace per-block click targeting with whole logical section targeting.
Wire persistent low-ceremony manual draft capture for editable sections.
Support structure-aware H2/H3/H4 insertion or section splitting.
Validate policy structure before draft capture.
Reuse the old/new lens review shape for drafts and proposal previews.
Keep broad style cleanup out of scope unless needed to make the workflow usable.
top_risks: The current SG-0014 review build targets individual rendered blocks and feels weird on click; revision must move the editing unit back to the old whole-section model.
Canonical Markdown writes should stay behind review/apply semantics; autosave drafts must not mutate source documents directly.
Section splitting and header insertion add structure-validation pressure, so the first revision should be conservative about allowed heading hierarchy.

changed_surfaces: service/archivist_service.py now keeps a single active editable section, preserves heading/list structure in section draft text, and prevents nested editable section wrappers
service/archivist_service.py keeps assembly, regulatory, artifact, code, and table surfaces static through contenteditable=false and excludes their content from editable draft hooks
src/main.tsx serializes active section edits as structured draft text, validates H2/H3/H4 hierarchy before draft capture, and removes the nested-section preview skip path
scripts/smoke_archivist.py now asserts the flat edit-section renderer contract, static-surface lockout, continuity-document section behavior, and browser consumption of a seeded draft review lens
residual_risks: Approved apply/write-back remains intentionally locked; canonical Markdown is not mutated by draft autosave.
The model proposal path is deterministic preview plumbing, not a live local-model call yet.
Heading insertion creates reviewable structured draft text inside the active editable section; final canonical Markdown section splitting still belongs to the later reviewed apply workflow.
Static structured surfaces are protected inside the section flow with contenteditable=false so the visual section remains coherent while static content stays out of draft hooks.

review_result.summary: Human review found the click/edit behavior odd because SG-0014 targeted individual rendered blocks. The previous manual browser treated editable blocks as whole logical sections, supported header insertion to create new sections, and used that structure to enforce policy shape. Revise SG-0014 around section-level editing before acceptance.

revision_result.summary: Correction pass implemented flat section metadata, static-surface lockout, structured draft serialization, and expanded service/browser smoke evidence. Human review found the edit chrome still feels wrong because the overlay sits on top of editable text, duplicates headings in the UI, and uses unclear text-label toolbar controls.

followup_review_result.summary: The section-level data model is closer, but the editing surface is visually intrusive. The current fixed edit halo and heading pill sit over the text and make the reader feel blocked even when pointer events pass through. The toolbar should move back to the old-browser pattern: a small edit affordance on the section halo/margin plus insertion controls between sections, not an oversized overlay on top of the paragraph.
requested_changes: Remove the selected section heading pill from the editing overlay; do not duplicate headings like H2 Purpose in UI chrome.
Remove or greatly reduce the big fixed edit outline that floats over the paragraph text; the editable text should remain directly clickable and readable.
Fix draft preview rendering so edited text does not break Markdown rendering; pending drafts must not replace rendered reader HTML with raw Markdown text like ## headings.

Allow only one active editable section at a time. Clicking into another section, clicking away, or otherwise leaving the active section must autosave the former section as a pending draft before any new section becomes editable.
Put the edit affordance on the section halo or margin, similar to the older browser, so the control is present but minimized.

Show the edit affordance on the section the user is moving toward or hovering, with a small comfortable cursor offset; it should feel anchored to the target section, not like it is chasing the pointer.
Only show bold, italic, paragraph, heading, list, and other formatting controls after the user explicitly clicks the edit affordance for a section.
Restore between-section insertion affordances: on margin/section-boundary hover, show a small control for inserting H2/H3/H4 between logical sections.
Replace raw letter/text toolbar buttons with intuitive office-style icon controls for edit, undo, bold, italic, paragraph, heading, bulleted list, numbered list, and insert section.
Keep section-level editing and autosaved draft review; this is a UI chrome correction, not a rollback to per-block editing.
likely_causes: src/styles.css positions .manual-edit-affordance absolutely over the document with a fixed-height .manual-edit-outline, so the editing chrome visually occludes the selected section.
src/main.tsx renders .manual-selected-block with the selected heading label, duplicating document headings in the editor UI.
src/main.tsx calls selectElementContents when edit mode starts, which reinforces the feeling that the whole block is captured instead of letting the user place the cursor naturally.

src/main.tsx currently previews pending drafts by assigning draft_text to section textContent, which causes Markdown heading markers and draft text to appear raw in the reader instead of being rendered back through the Markdown compatibility path.
The current edit affordance is a fixed toolbar tied to edit mode and selected state, not an anchored section-hover control with formatting tools hidden until edit activation.
The current toolbar uses B/I/P/H2/H3/H4/* text labels and a refresh icon for undo, which feels less like LibreOffice, Google Docs, or Office controls.
implementation_defaults: Use very liberal commit granularity as the repo grows: keep behavior fixes, UI chrome changes, smoke coverage, and project-brain evidence in small, reviewable commits instead of bundling multiple SG-0014 follow-up concerns together.

Preserve rendered Markdown in the normal reader and draft-preview states. Do not preview drafts by setting raw Markdown onto the section DOM; render draft text through a compatibility preview path or keep it in the review lens until a rendered preview exists.
Maintain a single active contenteditable section. Starting edit on a new section must flush the current section through the draft sidecar flow first, and blur/click-away should behave the same way.
Treat the section-hover edit affordance as a stable target attached to the section edge or margin with a small cursor-safe offset, not as a pointer-following floating toolbar.
Keep full formatting controls hidden until the user clicks edit; read/hover mode should expose only the minimal edit affordance and any between-section insert affordance.

changed_surfaces: src/main.tsx no longer assigns draft_text into editable section textContent for normal reader or edit-route draft preview states.
src/main.tsx undo now remounts the article from service-rendered HTML instead of writing original Markdown text back into the DOM.

scripts/smoke_archivist.py seeds a pending manual draft before browser routes and asserts normal reader/edit-mode DOM does not include the seeded draft text or raw ## heading markers while the draft review lens still shows the draft.
residual_risks: Pending draft text remains visible in the old/new review lens rather than being rendered inline in the article until a proper rendered draft preview path exists.
Single active editor click-away behavior, anchored hover edit affordance, between-section insertion controls, and toolbar iconography remain separate requested changes.

focused_build_passes.addressed_requested_change: Allow only one active editable section at a time. Clicking into another section, clicking away, or otherwise leaving the active section must autosave the former section as a pending draft before any new section becomes editable.
changed_surfaces: src/main.tsx now serializes section transitions through an awaited draft-save path before assigning a new contenteditable section.
src/main.tsx exposes editor transition state and active editable section metadata for browser evidence, and disables edit/heading controls while a draft transition is saving.

src/main.tsx adds an edit-switch smoke probe that appends text in one section, activates another section, and asserts the former section was saved as a pending manual draft while only one section remains contenteditable.
scripts/smoke_archivist.py adds an archivist-smoke=edit-switch browser route with screenshot evidence for single-active-editor autosave behavior.
residual_risks: Clicking away from the active section now uses the same autosave transition path; the browser smoke specifically covers switching from one editable section to another.
Anchored hover edit affordance, formatting toolbar hidden-until-edit behavior, between-section insertion affordances, and office-style iconography remain separate focused passes.

notes: This is the larger parity slice after the full browser shell exists. Renderer strategy is resolved: SG-0013 should expose service-rendered compatibility output first, then SG-0014 can deepen Markdown, artifact, editing, and proposal-review parity and promote high-value surfaces into React components.
